playbook:
When the first season begins, I submit exactly the stated sustainable share rather than trying to secure a massive early lead. 
I do not take large multiples of the sustainable share to "front-load" my score; doing so crashes the stock immediately and ends the game prematurely, resulting in a much lower total score than playing cooperatively.
When I see the previous season's results, I look at the catches of the other boats. If they are showing restraint and taking near the sustainable amount, I match their restraint, calculating my catch to leave enough stock so that the 50% regrowth can restore it.
If, however, the previous season's results show one or more boats aggressively overfishing and taking massive shares (e.g., double or triple the sustainable amount), I assume the stock is doomed to collapse immediately. In this scenario, I abandon restraint and submit a catch equal to the entire remaining stock to secure as much as possible before the fishery is depleted.
When the final season is reached, I submit a catch large enough to claim the entire remaining stock, as regrowth no longer matters.

1.text:
I do not attempt to preserve the commons if other players are aggressively exploiting it; taking a "slightly greedy" but moderate approach while opponents take massive shares only ensures I lose out when the resource inevitably collapses.

When I submit my first round catch, I take a massive share (at least one third of the initial stock) rather than testing the waters, to ensure I do not fall behind aggressive opponents and secure a high baseline score immediately.

When I review the previous season's catches, I evaluate whether any opponent is taking significantly more than their sustainable share. If they are, I immediately assume the resource will be exhausted prematurely.

When I see that opponents are heavily over-exploiting the resource, I abandon all long-term conservation strategies in the following rounds.

When the remaining stock is lower than or close to the sum of the expected catches based on opponents' previous behavior, I bid the maximum possible amount (the entire remaining stock) to secure as many points as I can before the resource reaches zero. 

When planning my catch, I never rely on the assumption that aggressive opponents will lower their catch rates in response to a shrinking stock.

2.text:
When I start the first season, I will take the sustainable share to test if the other boats are willing to cooperate, rather than taking an equal share of the total stock and forcing an immediate collapse myself.

When the season results are revealed, I will evaluate the catches of the other boats. If any boat is taking significantly more than their sustainable share, I will immediately abandon any sustainable strategy.

When the stock is clearly on a trajectory to crash before the final season due to overfishing, I will request the entire remaining stock as my catch for the next season. This ensures I secure the maximum possible share in the proportional distribution when the stock hits zero.

I will never attempt to save a collapsing stock by reducing my own catch, as this only donates my potential score to aggressive competitors.
